title: Temperature sensor fault
shortDescription: The temperature sensor is not sending a valid reading to the control board.
fullDescription:
Error E1 on a Bosch microwave means the cavity temperature sensor (thermistor) is either open, shorted, or out of range. The control board cannot safely run cooking cycles without an accurate temperature reading.

This often appears after spills, steam intrusion, or after a power surge. The oven will refuse to start or will abort a running program.

fixSteps.title: Power cycle
fixSteps.instruction: Unplug the microwave for 5 minutes, then plug back in and retry.

fixSteps.title: Inspect sensor harness
fixSteps.instruction: Remove the outer case and check that the thermistor plug is fully seated on the control board.

fixSteps.title: Test thermistor
fixSteps.instruction: Measure resistance at room temperature. Expect ~50kOhm at 25C; replace if open or shorted.

whenToCallPro: Call a pro if the harness and thermistor test good, which points to control board damage.

faq.q: Can I still use the microwave?
faq.a: No, the unit locks out heating until the sensor reads correctly.

title: Over-temperature in cavity
shortDescription: The control detected cavity temperature above the safe limit.
fullDescription:
E2 means the thermistor reported a temperature higher than the firmware allows, usually above 180C. The microwave trips to protect the magnetron and cavity.

Common causes are running with little or no food load, a stuck magnetron relay, or a blocked cooling fan that lets heat build up.
symptoms: E2 after several minutes of cooking

fixSteps.title: Let it cool
fixSteps.instruction: Leave the door open 30 minutes and restart the cycle.

fixSteps.title: Clean vents
fixSteps.instruction: Vacuum the top and rear vents; make sure nothing blocks the airflow.

fixSteps.title: Check cooling fan
fixSteps.instruction: With the case off, confirm the fan spins when the microwave runs.

whenToCallPro: Call a pro if the magnetron or HV circuit is suspected; those components carry lethal voltages.

faq.a: The lockout protects you. Do not bypass it.

title: Door switch fault
shortDescription: The door interlock switches are not reporting consistent open/closed states.
fullDescription:
E3 indicates the three door interlock switches are out of sequence. Bosch microwaves require primary, secondary, and monitor switches to change state together when the door is opened or closed.

One stuck switch, a bent door hook, or a misaligned latch will trigger this error and disable heating.

fixSteps.title: Check door fit
fixSteps.instruction: Close the door firmly and look for gaps at the hinges.

fixSteps.title: Test interlocks
fixSteps.instruction: With the control panel off, probe each microswitch for continuity in the correct state.

whenToCallPro: Call a pro if the door frame is bent, because door alignment affects safe microwave leakage.

faq.a: Safety redundancy so the magnetron cannot run with the door open.

title: Keypad or touch panel fault
shortDescription: The control detects a stuck key or an unresponsive touch panel.
fullDescription:
E4 appears when one or more buttons read as pressed for longer than expected, or when the capacitive touch panel is not communicating with the main board.

Moisture, grease, or a failed ribbon cable are the most common culprits. The microwave usually locks out until the key is released.

fixSteps.title: Dry the panel
fixSteps.instruction: Wipe the panel and let the unit sit unplugged for an hour.

fixSteps.title: Reseat ribbon
fixSteps.instruction: Remove the control assembly and reseat the flat ribbon cable into the main board.

whenToCallPro: Call a pro if the membrane under the glass is cracked; the whole assembly must be aligned precisely.

faq.q: Can I clean under the buttons?
faq.a: Not without disassembly; wipe the surface only.

title: Control board communication lost
shortDescription: The user interface board cannot talk to the main control board.
fullDescription:
E5 indicates a communication fault between the display/UI board and the relay/power board. Bosch uses a serial bus between these boards, and any break stops the microwave from starting.

Reseating the ribbon or connector fixes many cases. Persistent faults usually need a board swap.

fixSteps.title: Power reset
fixSteps.instruction: Unplug for 10 minutes and restart.

fixSteps.title: Reseat connectors
fixSteps.instruction: Open the cabinet and reseat all connectors between the UI and main boards.

whenToCallPro: Call a pro when both boards test good but the fault persists, to rule out wiring damage.

faq.q: Is it safe to keep trying?
faq.a: Yes, the microwave will not heat in this state.

title: Magnetron or HV circuit fault
shortDescription: The high-voltage circuit is not drawing expected current.
fullDescription:
E6 reflects an abnormal current reading on the HV circuit that powers the magnetron. The magnetron may be failing, or the HV diode, capacitor, or transformer may be bad.

Because this circuit stores lethal voltage even when unplugged, DIY repair is not recommended.

fixSteps.title: Power cycle
fixSteps.instruction: Unplug for 10 minutes and retry once.

fixSteps.title: Schedule service
fixSteps.instruction: Book a qualified technician to discharge the capacitor and test HV components.

whenToCallPro: Always call a pro; HV capacitors can kill even when unplugged.

faq.a: Yes, no radiation leakage occurs with this fault.

title: Main control board fault
shortDescription: The control board reports an internal self-test failure.
fullDescription:
F1 is a firmware self-test error. The main PCB has detected a memory or logic fault during startup and will not allow normal operation.

A power surge is the most common cause; sometimes a full power reset clears it, but usually the board needs replacement.

fixSteps.title: Hard reset
fixSteps.instruction: Unplug for 30 minutes and restart.

fixSteps.title: Replace board
fixSteps.instruction: Swap in a new main control board if the fault persists.

whenToCallPro: Call a pro if the replacement board also shows F1; wiring upstream may be the cause.

faq.a: Yes, plug the microwave into a surge-protected outlet after repair.

title: Relay stuck closed
shortDescription: A power relay on the main board is reading as permanently energized.
fullDescription:
F2 means the control board detects one of its relays, usually the magnetron or fan relay, is stuck in the closed position when it should be open. To protect the unit, the microwave locks out.

A stuck relay is a fire risk because it can keep powering components after the cycle ends.

fixSteps.title: Unplug immediately
fixSteps.instruction: Disconnect the microwave from power.

fixSteps.title: Replace main board
fixSteps.instruction: Install a new main control board; individual relay replacement is not supported.

whenToCallPro: Call a pro if you are not comfortable working inside a microwave; discharge the HV cap first.

faq.q: Is it safe to keep using?

title: Humidity sensor fault
shortDescription: The humidity sensor used for auto-cook is out of range.
fullDescription:
F4 is limited to Bosch microwaves with sensor cooking. It means the humidity sensor reads an invalid value at startup or during a cycle.

Grease buildup on the sensor is the most common cause. Clean first; replace if cleaning does not help.

fixSteps.title: Clean sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Locate the sensor port on the cavity wall and wipe with a damp microfiber cloth.

fixSteps.title: Replace sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Swap the sensor module if cleaning does not clear the error.

whenToCallPro: Call a pro if you are not confident separating the cavity liner to reach the sensor.

faq.a: Yes, manual power and time settings still work.

title: Turntable motor fault
shortDescription: The turntable motor is not turning as expected.
fullDescription:
F5 indicates the turntable motor has stalled or the feedback signal is missing. Only Bosch microwaves with sensor feedback on the motor detect this directly; others just stop rotating silently.

A foreign object under the plate or a seized motor are the typical causes.

fixSteps.title: Clear the tray
fixSteps.instruction: Remove the glass tray and roller ring and wash both; vacuum the hub.

fixSteps.title: Replace motor
fixSteps.instruction: Access the motor from the bottom of the cavity and swap it.

whenToCallPro: Call a pro if the motor tests good and the hub still will not turn.

faq.q: Can I use it without rotation?
faq.a: Heating will be uneven but functional.

title: Line voltage out of range
shortDescription: The control board detects a supply voltage outside acceptable limits.
fullDescription:
F6 means the mains voltage was too low or too high during operation. Shared circuits with heavy appliances, or utility brownouts, commonly trigger this fault.

The microwave self-protects by locking out until voltage recovers.

fixSteps.title: Move to another outlet
fixSteps.instruction: Try a dedicated 15A outlet on a different circuit.

fixSteps.title: Measure voltage
fixSteps.instruction: Check the outlet reads 110-125V under load.

whenToCallPro: Call an electrician if voltage is abnormal; it is a wiring, not an appliance, issue.

title: Overcurrent protection tripped
shortDescription: The microwave sensed a current spike and opened its internal fuse.
fullDescription:
F7 indicates an overcurrent event. The microwave may recover after a cool-down, but repeated F7 codes point to a short or a failing component such as the HV capacitor or magnetron.

The inline thermal fuse may also have opened.

fixSteps.title: Cool down
fixSteps.instruction: Leave the microwave unplugged for 30 minutes.

fixSteps.title: Inspect fuse
fixSteps.instruction: A technician should test the thermal and line fuses with the HV capacitor discharged.

whenToCallPro: Always call a pro for repeat F7 events; HV capacitors can be lethal.

faq.q: Should I keep trying to start it?
faq.a: No, repeat attempts may damage the board.
